### "Exodus" -- the high-contrast alternatives

Where six related hues will not separate, the guide swaps in the `bright` and
`dark` supporting sets (p.11).

```{r exodus, econ_height = 185}
## The guide spaces its four dates by eye, not by years, so positions are
## read off the chart.
dates <- c(172, 406, 522.5, 584)
countries <- c("Egypt", "Syria", "Palestine", "Israel", "Iraq", "U.A.E", "Saudi Arabia")
mideast <- data.frame(
  date = rep(dates, 7),
  country = factor(rep(countries, each = 4), levels = countries),
  pct = c(
    18.7, 15.9, 10.2, 8.6, 15.6, 9.7, 5.2, 2.6, 11.6, 4.7, 1.9, 1.1, 8.1, 2.8, 2.5, 1.8,
    6.3, 3.7, 1.4, 0.7, 0.1, 5.9, 12.7, 12.7, 0, 0.4, 4.4, 4.5
  )
)

## The chart's own colours: cyan, teal, purple (bright 1), blue, mint, pink, orange (bright 3).
country_cols <- c(
  pal_line(2)[2], pal_line(5)[5], economist_2017_pal("print", set = "bright")(1), pal_line(1),
  pal_stack(6)[5], "#DD5566", economist_2017_pal("print", set = "bright")(3)[3]
)

exodus <- ggplot(mideast, aes(date, pct, colour = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, key_glyph = "rect") +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 20)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(172, 650), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = dates, labels = c("1910", "70", "2010", "25*")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = country_cols, labels = c(countries[-7], "Saudi\nArabia")) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Exodus",
    subtitle = "Christians, as % of population",
    x = "Available years", y = NULL, colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "left", legend.direction = "vertical", legend.justification = "top",
    legend.key.spacing.y = unit(6, "pt")
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  exodus +
    labs(caption = paste0(
      "Source: \u201cOngoing Exodus: Tracking the\nEmigration of Christians from the Middle\n",
      "East\u201d by T. Johnson and G. Zurlo, 2015"
    )),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Forecast"
)
```

## Lines, stacked (p.16)

Stacked areas take the `stacked` order. Where a band is wide enough, the
guide labels it in place in white rather than using a key.

### "Foreign hoards" -- two bands, labeled in place

```{r foreign-hoards, econ_height = 154}
china <- c(
  0.26, 0.36, 0.56, 0.77, 1.02, 1.49, 1.91, 2.3, 2.64, 2.96
)
other <- c(
  0.77, 0.98, 1.23, 1.51, 2.03, 2.86, 3.02, 3.19, 3.54, 3.77
)
reserves <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2002:2011, 2),
  trn = c(china, other),
  region = factor(rep(c("China", "Other developing countries"), each = 10),
                  levels = c("China", "Other developing countries"))
)

## A white rule runs along the top of every band but the last, which borders
## the ground: its colour is NA.
hoards <- ggplot(reserves, aes(year, trn, fill = region, colour = region)) +
  geom_area(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), outline.type = "upper", linewidth = 0.3) +
  annotate("text", x = 2010, y = 1.18, label = "China",
           colour = "white", size = 2.8, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 2009.4, y = 4.3, label = "Other\ndeveloping\ncountries",
           colour = "white", size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 6.8),
                     breaks = seq(0, 6, 2), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(2001.52, 2012), breaks = c(2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2011),
                     labels = c("2002", "04", "06", "08", "10*", "11*")) +
  scale_fill_economist_2017("print", type = "stacked", guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("white", NA), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Foreign hoards",
    subtitle = "Developing-country currency reserves\n$trn",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print")

economist_2017_chart(
  hoards +
    labs(caption = "Source: IMF"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Forecast"
)
```

### "The big shift" -- six bands with a key

```{r big-shift, econ_height = 178}

shift_bands <- list(

    4.3, 5.2, 3.8, 5.2, 7.3, 7.3, 5.5, 5.7, 6.9, 6.8, 5.9, 4, 8, 8.3, 10.1, 11, 11, 11.7, 9.9, 9.8, 9.2, 9.9, 12.9,

  ),

  ),

    5.6, 5.6, 5.3, 6, 7.6, 5.4, 6.5, 7.9
  ),
  Ireland = c(
    2.2, 2.2, 2.6, 2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 3, 3.6, 3.2, 2.3, 2.3, 2.1, 2.3, 4.9, 3.7, 4.4, 4.7, 5.1, 5.4, 6.2,
    6.3, 6, 6.2, 7.6, 7.4, 6.3, 7, 8.8, 7.9
  ),
  Singapore = c(
    1.9, 1.9, 1.8, 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.6, 1.4, 1.9, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3, 3.2, 3, 3, 3.3, 1.9, 2.3, 3, 3, 3.5, 3.5, 3.7, 5.8,
    5.1, 5.4, 4.4, 3, 4, 4.9, 4.9, 5.1
  ),
  Switzerland = c(
    6, 5.4, 5.4, 5.3, 5.6, 6.9, 5.4, 7.2, 7.7, 6.3, 5.6, 7.4, 6.9, 4.9, 4.9, 4.9, 7, 6, 4, 6.3, 8.8, 7.9, 6.7, 5.8,

shift <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(shift_bands), function(haven) {

    year = 1982:2013,
    haven = factor(haven, levels = names(shift_bands)),

  )

## The key runs down into the top of the panel, with the gridlines stopped at
## its edge: a ground-coloured block under the areas but over the gridlines.
big_shift <- ggplot(shift, aes(year, pct, fill = haven, colour = haven)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1980.2, xmax = 2005.5, ymin = 56, ymax = 60.5, fill = print_bg) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1980.2, xmax = 1994, ymin = 28, ymax = 54.5, fill = print_bg) +
```

### "In limbo" -- the alternative stacked scheme

The guide supplies a second five-color order "for use where categories are
chronological or where primary colour scheme doesn't work" (p.16).

```{r in-limbo, econ_height = 185}
## Band thicknesses, bottom to top, read off the guide.
tenure_bands <- list(
  `Private rental` = c(
    6.4, 4.8, 7.3, 5.8, 8.6, 9.2, 8.9, 10.2, 9.8, 10.2, 11.4, 8.3, 6.1, 6.1, 7, 9.2, 13, 17.7
  ),
  `Private leased by LA/HA*` = c(
    12.5, 15.9, 16.9, 21.9, 20.6, 27.5, 40.9, 46.6, 49.7, 47.2, 40.9, 38.1, 31.6, 27.5, 25.9, 26.2, 25.3, 23.4
  ),
  `LA/HA*` = c(
    14.1, 18.4, 21.2, 25.3, 27.2, 27.8, 27.8, 26.9, 23.1, 18.1, 15.3, 10.9, 8.1, 7.2, 8.1, 9.1, 9.7, 10.3
  ),
  Hostel = c(
    9.7, 10, 10, 10.6, 10, 10, 10.6, 10.3, 9.1, 7.8, 6.6, 5.3, 4.1, 4.4, 4.4, 4.4, 4.7, 5
  ),
  `Bed & breakfast` = c(
    5.3, 7.2, 9.1, 11.2, 12.8, 13.4, 8.1, 6.9, 5.6, 4.7, 4.4, 3.1, 2.5, 2.8, 3.8, 4.1, 4.4, 5
  )
)
limbo <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(tenure_bands), function(tenure) {
  data.frame(
    year = 1998:2015,
    tenure = factor(tenure, levels = names(tenure_bands)),
    n = tenure_bands[[tenure]]
  )
}))

## The guide's alternative order: blue, cyan, teal, mauve, maroon.
alt_stack <- c(pal_stack(6)[1], pal_stack(6)[2], pal_stack(6)[4],
               pal_bar(6)[6], pal_bar(6)[5])

limbo_plot <- ggplot(limbo, aes(year, n, fill = tenure, colour = tenure)) +
  geom_area(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), outline.type = "upper", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 102),
                     breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(1997.56, 2017.1),
                     breaks = c(1998, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2015), minor_breaks = 1998:2015,
                     labels = c("1998", "2002", "04", "06", "08", "10", "12", "15"),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = alt_stack) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(rep("white", 4), NA), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "In limbo",
    subtitle = "Households in temporary homes\nEngland, \u2019000",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.7))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_2017_chart(
  limbo_plot +
    labs(caption = "Source: DCLG"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Local authorities and\nhousing associations"
)
```

### "Emerging middle class" -- four bands, labeled in place

```{r emerging-middle, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 234}
fn <- economist_2017_footnote(1:3)
extremely_poor <- c(
  0.88, 0.88, 0.87, 0.79, 0.7, 0.72, 0.73, 0.74, 0.72, 0.71, 0.7, 0.67, 0.61, 0.57, 0.52, 0.51, 0.48, 0.47, 0.45,
  0.43, 0.38, 0.35, 0.34, 0.33, 0.32, 0.31
)
moderately_poor <- c(
  0.35, 0.37, 0.39, 0.44, 0.48, 0.5, 0.5, 0.49, 0.51, 0.52, 0.53, 0.53, 0.54, 0.53, 0.53, 0.53, 0.52, 0.5, 0.5, 0.48,
  0.47, 0.46, 0.45, 0.44, 0.43, 0.43
)
near_poor <- c(
  0.2, 0.22, 0.24, 0.28, 0.32, 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, 0.36, 0.37, 0.39, 0.41, 0.44, 0.47, 0.49, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5,
  0.52, 0.53, 0.53, 0.53, 0.53, 0.53
)
developing_middle <- c(
  0.27, 0.28, 0.29, 0.3, 0.33, 0.33, 0.35, 0.36, 0.39, 0.41, 0.44, 0.47, 0.52, 0.57, 0.61, 0.65, 0.7, 0.73, 0.77,
  0.81, 0.87, 0.9, 0.94, 0.97, 1, 1.01
)
developed_middle <- c(
  0.14, 0.13, 0.13, 0.13, 0.14, 0.14, 0.14, 0.14, 0.14, 0.15, 0.15, 0.16, 0.17, 0.2, 0.21, 0.23, 0.26, 0.28, 0.29,
  0.31, 0.33, 0.37, 0.39, 0.42, 0.44, 0.47
)
classes <- c("Extremely poor", "Moderately poor", "Near poor", "Developing middle class", "Developed middle class")
emerging <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1991:2016, 5),
  class = factor(rep(classes, each = 26), levels = classes),
  bn = c(extremely_poor, moderately_poor, near_poor, developing_middle, developed_middle)
)

## Each band is named in bold with its income range under it; the labels sit
## where the guide puts them, light on the dark bands and dark on the light.
band_labels <- data.frame(
  year = c(1992.02, 1997.67, 2003.43, 2007.2, 2013.1, 2015.73, 2015.73),
  bn = c(0.43, 1.04, 1.42, 1.91, 2.37, 2.52, 2.37),
  label = c("Extremely poor", "Moderately poor", "Near poor", "Developing middle class",
            "class and above", "Developed middle", "over $13"),
  face = c(rep("bold", 6), "plain"),
  colour = c("white", ink, "white", ink, "white", "white", "white"),
  hjust = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1)
)
band_ranges <- data.frame(
  year = c(1992.02, 1997.67, 2003.43, 2007.2),
  bn = c(0.28, 0.9, 1.27, 1.77),
  label = c("less than $1.90", "$1.90 to $3.10", "$3.11 to $5", "$5.01 to $13"),
  colour = c("white", ink, "white", ink)
)

emerging_plot <- ggplot(emerging, aes(year, bn, fill = class, colour = class)) +
  geom_area(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), outline.type = "upper", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(
    data = band_labels, aes(year, bn, label = label, hjust = hjust, fontface = face),
    colour = band_labels$colour, size = 2.6, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = band_ranges, aes(year, bn, label = label),
    colour = band_ranges$colour, size = 2.6, hjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 3),
                     breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.5), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1.0", "1.5", "2.0", "2.5", "3.0"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(1990.41, 2017.5), minor_breaks = 1991:2016,
                     breaks = c(1991, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2016),
                     ## The fallback font is too wide for "15" and "16" side by
                     ## side, so 2015 keeps its tick but not its label.
                     labels = c("1991", "95", "2000", "05", "10", "", paste0("16", fn[3])),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = alt_stack, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(rep("white", 4), NA), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Emerging middle class",
    subtitle = paste0("Working population by economic class, emerging and developing countries", fn[1],
                      ", 2011$ at PPP", fn[2], ", bn"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print")

economist_2017_chart(
  emerging_plot +
    labs(caption = "Source: ILO"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = paste0(
    fn[1], "Excluding most Western developed countries  ",
    fn[2], "Purchasing-power parity  ", fn[3], "Estimate"
  )
)
```

## Thermometer (p.17)

Not a `ggplot2` geom, but structurally a range between two or more values per
category. The guide draws terminals as short vertical rules, and repeats the
same chart at two, three, four and six series to show the color order --
with the note that "any more than 4 categories is probably too many and you
should have a rethink".

```{r thermometer-data}
fields <- c("Mathematics", "Economics", "Computer Science", "Business", "Biology",
            "Philosophy", "English", "Psychology", "History", "Communication")
series_names <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")

## Per series values, read off the guide's marks. The guide redraws the data
## for each series count, so each chart has its own table (one row per field).
thermo_values <- list(
  `2` = list(
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33),
    c(416, 398, 382, 316, 308, 275, 290, 239, 283, 251)
  ),
  `3` = list(
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33),
    c(418, 398, 382, 316, 308, 275, 290, 239, 283, 251),
    c(395, 316, 292, 266, 257, 215, 201, 199, 197, 187)
  ),
  `4` = list(
    c(280, 249, 117, 191, 84, 148, 80, 60, 134, 121),
    c(402, 316, 292, 266, 257, 214, 201, 199, 197, 187),
    c(339, 397, 381, 315, 307, 275, 290, 239, 283, 250),
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33)
  ),
  `6` = list(
    c(222, 191, 172, 133, 16, 180, 152, 104, 233, 109),
    c(405, 398, 382, 316, 308, 276, 290, 238, 284, 251),
    c(280, 249, 117, 192, 84, 147, 80, 60, 135, 121),
    c(31, 40, 72, 37, 39, 43, 35, 15, 21, 34),
    c(335, 294, 134, 236, 129, 196, 52, 199, 260, 156),
    c(375, 317, 292, 266, 257, 214, 201, 199, 197, 187)
  ),
  dot = list(
    c(31, 41, 72, 37, 39, 43, 35, 15, 21, 34),
    c(419, 398, 382, 280, 308, 276, 290, 239, 284, 251),
    c(396, 317, 364, 263, 257, 215, 201, 222, 197, 187)
  )
)

thermo_data <- function(key) {
  values <- thermo_values[[key]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(values), function(k) {
    data.frame(
      field = factor(fields, levels = rev(fields)),
      series = factor(series_names[k], levels = series_names),
      value = values[[k]]
    )
  }))
}

## The connecting rule runs from the zero axis to the highest series.
thermo_plot <- function(n, terminals = c("rule", "dot")) {
  terminals <- match.arg(terminals)
  d <- thermo_data(if (terminals == "dot") "dot" else as.character(n))
  spans <- aggregate(value ~ field, d, max)

  ## The rule is the grid's own blue, a step darker; darker again under dots.
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(y = .data$field)) +
    geom_segment(data = spans, aes(x = 0, xend = .data$value, y = .data$field, yend = .data$field),
                 colour = if (terminals == "rule") "#92A9B4" else "#66808E", linewidth = 0.47)
  p <- p + if (terminals == "rule") {
    ## Vertical rules about 2pt wide and 0.8 of a row tall, the guide's default terminal.
    geom_linerange(aes(x = .data$value, ymin = as.numeric(.data$field) - 0.41,
                       ymax = as.numeric(.data$field) + 0.41, colour = .data$series),
                   linewidth = 1, key_glyph = "vline")
  } else {
    geom_point(aes(x = .data$value, colour = .data$series), size = 1.6)
  }

  ## "Horrible" sits on the axis-number row at the left edge of the category labels, the
  ## width of the longest label to the left of the panel.
  label_gp <- gpar(fontsize = 7, fontface = "bold")
  p +
    annotation_custom(textGrob(
      "\u201cHorrible\u201d", gp = label_gp, hjust = 0, vjust = 0,
      x = unit(0, "npc") - grobWidth(textGrob("Computer Science", gp = gpar(fontsize = 7))) + unit(1.5, "pt"),
      y = unit(1, "npc") + unit(2, "pt")
    )) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(0, 425), breaks = seq(0, 400, 100),
                       expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "dot") +
    labs(
      title = "The horrible science",
      subtitle = paste0("Use of specific \u201cadjective\u201d per million\n",
                        "words in student reviews on\n",
                        "RateMyProfessors.com*"),
      x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL
    ) +
    theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE) +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25))
}
```

## Scatter (p.18)

The guide is specific about marks: standard dots 4px at 50% opacity "where
general trend is more important than individual point", highlight dots at
100% opacity "to label outliers / important data points", category dots with
a 0.3px stroke and 50% fill for bubble charts, and trend lines at 1px, dashed
3px/1px.

### Chart elements

```{r scatter-elements, econ_size = "one_column", econ_height = 410}
## The specimen is laid out in points, as the guide prints it: one data unit is
## one point, measured from the top left of the specimen.
spec_x <- function(px) (px - 30) * 0.2566
spec_y <- function(py) 410 - (py - 15) * 0.2566
blue <- pal_dot(6)[4]
red <- pal_dot(6)[2]
gold <- pal_dot(6)[3]
cyan <- pal_dot(6)[1]

## Dot specimens: three overlapping dots per row. Diameters are the guide's, in points.
dots <- data.frame(
  x = spec_x(rep(c(66, 102, 139), 6)),
  y = spec_y(rep(c(289, 665, 766, 1061, 1168, 1275), each = 3)),
  size = c(rep(72, 3 * 3), rep(c(36, 52, 76), 3)) * 0.2566 / 0.75 / ggplot2::.pt,
  colour = rep(c(cyan, blue, red, blue, red, gold), each = 3),
  kind = rep(c("standard", "highlight", "highlight", "category", "category", "category"), each = 3)
)
standard <- dots$kind == "standard"
highlight <- dots$kind == "highlight"
category <- dots$kind == "category"

notes <- data.frame(
  x = spec_x(219),
  y = spec_y(c(286, 337, 392, 445, 489, 531, 663, 714, 768, 822, 865,
               1055, 1105, 1160, 1214, 1257, 1483, 1533, 1588)),
  label = c("Standard dot", "4px width", "50% opacity",
            "use where general trend", "is more important than", "individual point",
            "highlight dot", "4px width", "100% opacity",
            "use to label outliers /", "important data points",
            "Category dot", "0.3px stroke", "50% opacity fill",
            "use for bubble charts", "to differential colours",
            "trend lines", "1px stroke", "dashed 3px, 1px"),
  face = c("bold", "plain", "plain", rep("italic", 3), "bold", "plain", "plain", rep("italic", 2),
           "bold", "plain", "plain", rep("italic", 2), "bold", "plain", "plain")
)

ggplot() +
  ## Standard dots, 50% opacity, so overlaps darken.
  geom_point(data = dots[standard, ], aes(x, y, size = size), colour = "transparent", fill = alpha(cyan, 0.5),
             shape = 21) +
  ## Highlight dots, 100% opacity with a hairline white edge to separate overlaps.
  geom_point(data = dots[highlight, ], aes(x, y, size = size, fill = colour), colour = "white",
             shape = 21, stroke = 0.2) +
  ## Category dots, 50% fill with a 0.3px stroke in the full colour.
  geom_point(data = dots[category, ], aes(x, y, size = size, colour = colour), shape = 21,
             fill = NA, stroke = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = dots[category, ], aes(x, y, size = size, fill = alpha(colour, 0.5)),
             colour = "transparent", shape = 21) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = spec_x(58), xend = spec_x(193), y = spec_y(1485), yend = spec_y(1485)),
               colour = red, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "31") +
  geom_text(data = notes, aes(x, y, label = label, fontface = face), hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = spec_y(42), label = "Chart elements", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 4.9) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 160), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 410), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed(clip = "off") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

### "Divergent" -- standard scatter with trend lines

```{r divergent, econ_height = 195}
set.seed(2017)
## The 1990-2007 cloud is tight and steep; the 2012-16 cloud is wide and flat.
## Five 1990-2007 outliers sit out to the right.
metro_old <- data.frame(employment = rnorm(240, 1.6, 1.1))
metro_old$house_prices <- 1.3 + 2.2 * metro_old$employment + rnorm(240, 0, 1.8)
metro_old <- rbind(metro_old, data.frame(employment = c(4.4, 4.8, 5.1, 5.9, 8.2),
                                         house_prices = c(2.8, 8.2, 7.9, 7.6, 6.6)))
metro_new <- data.frame(employment = rnorm(210, 2.1, 1.6))
metro_new$house_prices <- 3.5 + 0.67 * metro_new$employment + rnorm(210, 0, 3.9)

periods <- c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007", "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016")
metro <- rbind(
  cbind(period = periods[2], metro_new),
  cbind(period = periods[1], metro_old)
)
metro$period <- factor(metro$period, levels = periods)

## Trend lines run over the span the guide draws them.
trends <- data.frame(
  period = factor(periods, levels = periods),
  x = c(-1.5, -0.7), xend = c(5.8, 8.2),
  y = c(-2, 3), yend = c(14.2, 9)
)

divergent <- ggplot(metro, aes(employment, house_prices, colour = period)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = trends, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = trends, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = "black",
               linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "31") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.4, 8.8), ylim = c(-5, 20), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-2, 8, 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", breaks = seq(-5, 20, 5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007" = pal_dot(2)[2], "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016" = pal_dot(1))) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2.2, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Divergent",
    subtitle = "United States, housing and employment\nMetro areas*, average annual change, %",
    x = "Employment", y = "House prices", colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = grid_col), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

economist_2017_chart(
  divergent +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Freddie Mac;\nUS Bureau of Labour Statistics"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*At least\n100,000 population"
)
```

### "The best disinfectant" -- labeled outliers

Standard dots carry the cloud; highlight dots at full opacity carry the
labels. The guide's note here: "sub title should summarise chart, save
specific units for axis labels".

```{r disinfectant, econ_height = 166}
set.seed(11)
## A diffuse cloud of countries, plus a denser band of more open, less corrupt ones.
corruption <- data.frame(open = c(runif(55, 19, 63), runif(24, 60, 92)))
corruption$score <- c(
  pmin(55, pmax(5, 0.55 * (corruption$open[1:55] - 19) + 10 + rnorm(55, 0, 13))),
  runif(24, 33, 70)
)
named <- data.frame(
  country = c("Britain", "Denmark", "India", "Colombia", "US", "Sweden", "Mexico", "Singapore"),
  open = c(77.5, 91.7, 37.8, 37, 73.8, 86.8, 34.9, 83.7),
  score = c(96.5, 82.5, 67.4, 66, 69.6, 65.6, 53, 34.4),
  ## Where each label sits, relative to its dot, in data units.
  lx = c(76, 84.5, 42.8, 34.1, 70.9, 95.2, 19.6, 83.7),
  ly = c(91, 91, 75.4, 67.4, 70.2, 50, 52.6, 26.7),
  hjust = c(1, 0, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.5, 1, 0.5)
)
## Leader lines for the two labels that sit away from their dots.
leaders <- data.frame(x = c(20.5, 86.8, 92.6), xend = c(34.9, 92.6, 92.6),
                      y = c(53, 65.6, 65.6), yend = c(53, 65.6, 55))

disinfectant <- ggplot(corruption, aes(open, score)) +
  geom_point(colour = pal_dot(1), size = 1.4) +
  geom_segment(data = leaders, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = pal_dot(2)[2],
               linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = named, colour = pal_dot(2)[2], size = 1.4) +
  geom_text(data = named, aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = country, hjust = hjust), size = 2.3, colour = "#5B6770") +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 100),
                     breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 115), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "The best disinfectant",
    subtitle = "Corruption and open data",
    x = "Corruption-perceptions index score, 2014\n100=least corrupt",
    y = "Open-data index score,\nlatest, 100=most open"
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = grid_col),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

economist_2017_chart(
  disinfectant +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Transparency International;\nOpen Knowledge Foundation"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### "Right nation" -- connected scatter

Two observations per country, joined. "To avoid obscuring the connecting
lines and labels, axis lines can be broken" (p.18).

```{r right-nation, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 234}
## The seven labelled countries, joined from 2003 to 2013, read off the guide.
oecd <- data.frame(
  country = rep(c("Japan", "France", "Britain", "Germany", "Chile", "Turkey", "United States"), 2),
  year = rep(c("2003", "2013*"), each = 7),
  spend = c(2.2, 2.83, 2.35, 3.06, 0.78, 0.44, 5.76,
            3.7, 4.11, 3.35, 4.78, 1.6, 0.94, 8.72),
  life = c(81.3, 78.7, 77.9, 78.1, 76.7, 71.8, 76.6,
           83.0, 81.8, 80.6, 80.4, 78.3, 76.0, 78.3)
)
oecd$year <- factor(oecd$year, levels = c("2003", "2013*"))

## The other OECD countries, as faint dots (also read off the guide).
others <- rbind(
  data.frame(year = "2003", spend = c(3.19, 3.78, 2.55, 2.8, 2.23, 1.66, 1.85, 1.95, 2.92, 3.59, 2.84, 2.84, 2.16,
                                      3.36, 1.76, 2.78, 1.0, 1.69, 1.29, 0.68, 0.76, 0.78, 1.27, 0.65),
             life = c(80.5, 80.1, 80.0, 80.0, 79.6, 79.2, 79.3, 78.7, 79.2, 79.1, 78.2, 77.6, 78.0,
                      77.3, 77.0, 76.9, 76.8, 75.9, 74.8, 74.2, 74.1, 73.3, 72.1, 71.3)),
  data.frame(year = "2013*", spend = c(2.9, 6.26, 3.06, 3.86, 2.39, 3.67, 4.9, 4.37, 5.86, 2.36, 4.35, 2.35, 3.32,
                                       5.13, 4.55, 3.68, 2.51, 4.25, 4.55, 2.03, 1.55, 2.01, 1.72, 1.05, 2.33),
             life = c(82.7, 82.4, 82.4, 81.7, 81.7, 81.6, 81.5, 81.4, 81.3, 81.3, 81.0, 80.9, 81.0,
                      80.9, 80.7, 80.5, 80.3, 80.2, 79.8, 77.8, 76.9, 76.0, 75.2, 74.1, 73.6))
)
others$year <- factor(others$year, levels = levels(oecd$year))

## Labels, ranged against their dots as the guide sets them.
nation_labels <- data.frame(
  country = c("Japan", "France", "Britain", "Germany", "Chile", "Turkey", "United States"),
  x = c(2.05, 4.48, 2.31, 5.2, 0.65, 0.38, 5.63),
  y = c(81.4, 82.3, 77.05, 79.1, 76.5, 72.4, 76.5),
  hjust = c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 1),
  face = c(rep("plain", 6), "bold")
)

## Gridlines are broken to leave the lines and labels clear: the top and bottom
## rules run the full width, the rest only in the margins.
rule_y <- c(70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 82)
broken_grid <- data.frame(
  x = rep(c(-0.8, 9.35), each = length(rule_y)), xend = rep(c(-0.2, 10), each = length(rule_y)),
  y = rep(rule_y, 2)
)

right_nation <- ggplot(oecd, aes(spend, life)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(68, 84), colour = grid_col, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_segment(data = broken_grid, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), colour = grid_col,
               linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = others, aes(colour = year), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(group = country), colour = "#6F909D", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = year), size = 1.6) +
  geom_text(data = nation_labels, aes(x = x, y = y, label = country, hjust = hjust, fontface = face),
            size = 2.3, colour = "#5B6770", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  annotate("segment", x = 4.82, xend = 4.82, y = 80.3, yend = 79.5, linewidth = 0.2, colour = "#5B6770") +
  ## The 2013 averages, called out with dashed rules and labels.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80.5, linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3.45, linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.25) +
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = 80.85, label = "bold('2013 average')~'80.5'", parse = TRUE,
           size = 2.5, hjust = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.55, y = c(70.5, 69.6), label = c("2013", "average"), size = 2.5, hjust = 0,
           fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 3.55, y = 68.7, label = "$3,453", size = 2.5, hjust = 0) +
  ## A connected key, in place of a legend.
  annotate("segment", x = 1.98, xend = 2.65, y = 85.2, yend = 85.2, colour = "#8E3150", linewidth = 0.25) +
  annotate("point", x = c(1.98, 2.65), y = 85.2, colour = pal_dot(2)[c(1, 2)], size = 1.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 1.87, y = 85.2, label = "2003", hjust = 1, size = 2.5, colour = pal_dot(2)[1]) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.8, y = 85.2, label = "2013*", hjust = 0, size = 2.5, colour = pal_dot(2)[2]) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.8, 10), ylim = c(68, 84), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  ## 80 is left off, where the average label sits.
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", breaks = c(70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 82, 84)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:9) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "dot", guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Right nation",
    subtitle = "Health spending and life expectancy at birth\nOECD countries",
    x = "Health expenditures per person\nat purchasing-power parity, current prices, $'000",
    y = "Life expectancy,\nyears"
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5), panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

economist_2017_chart(
  right_nation +
    labs(caption = "Source: OECD"),
```

### "Vitality and the vote" -- bubble chart, four categories

Category dots: 50% opacity fill with a thin stroke, sized by a second
variable.

```{r vitality, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 275}
set.seed(4)
regions <- c("Northeast", "Midwest", "West", "South")
## Per region: number of counties, health score mean and spread, swing at the mean health, and
## how large the counties are (log-mean of voting-eligible population).
region_spec <- data.frame(
  region = regions, n = c(150, 700, 70, 450),
  health_mean = c(42, 37.5, 50, 47), health_sd = c(6, 5, 8, 9),
  swing_mean = c(12, 15, -2, 5), swing_sd = c(7, 9, 11, 8), size_mean = c(1.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.8)
)
counties <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(region_spec)), function(i) {
  r <- region_spec[i, ]
  health <- pmin(66, pmax(22, rnorm(r$n, r$health_mean, r$health_sd)))
  data.frame(
    region = r$region,
    health = health,
    swing = r$swing_mean - 1 * (health - r$health_mean) + rnorm(r$n, 0, r$swing_sd),
    pop = rlnorm(r$n, r$size_mean, 0.75)
  )
}))
## Drawn from the southern cloud up, so the Midwest and Northeast lie on top.
counties$region <- factor(counties$region, levels = c("South", "West", "Midwest", "Northeast"))
counties <- counties[order(counties$region), ]
counties$region <- factor(counties$region, levels = regions)

region_cols <- c(Northeast = pal_dot(6)[4], Midwest = pal_dot(6)[2], West = pal_dot(6)[3], South = pal_dot(6)[1])

## The notes the guide hangs around the panel: arrows along the swing axis and
## either end of the health axis. Offsets are in points, from the panel edge. (The guide sets
## the swing arrows outside the panel; there is no room for them beyond the figure edge here.)
note_col <- "#7C8F9B"
note_gp <- gpar(fontsize = 5.5, col = note_col)
arrow_note <- function(label, y, up) {
  grobTree(
    textGrob(label, x = unit(0, "npc") + unit(5, "pt"), y = unit(y, "npc"), rot = 90, gp = note_gp),
    polygonGrob(
      x = unit(0, "npc") + unit(5, "pt") + unit(c(-2.2, 2.2, 0), "pt"),
      y = unit(if (up) 0.985 else 0.015, "npc") + unit(if (up) c(0, 0, 4.4) else c(4.4, 4.4, 0), "pt") -
        unit(if (up) 4.4 else 2.2, "pt"),
      gp = gpar(fill = note_col, col = NA)
    )
  )
}
health_note <- function(label, left) {
  tip <- if (left) 0 else 1
  grobTree(
    textGrob(label, x = unit(tip, "npc") + unit(if (left) 7 else -7, "pt"), y = unit(0, "npc") - unit(14, "pt"),
             hjust = if (left) 0 else 1, gp = note_gp),
    polygonGrob(
      x = unit(tip, "npc") + unit(if (left) c(0, 4.4, 4.4) else c(0, -4.4, -4.4), "pt"),
      y = unit(0, "npc") + unit(c(-14, -11.8, -16.2), "pt"),
      gp = gpar(fill = note_col, col = NA)
    )
  )
}

## The key, drawn inside the panel at the top right: regions, then dot size.
vitality_key <- function(show_regions = TRUE) {
  region_key <- if (show_regions) {
    list(
      annotate("text", x = 61.1, y = 43.6, label = "Region", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 2.5),
      annotate("point", x = 61.1, y = c(38, 32.9, 27.4, 22.7), shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.3,
               colour = region_cols[c(1, 2, 3, 4)], fill = alpha(region_cols[c(1, 2, 3, 4)], 0.5)),
      annotate("text", x = 62.4, y = c(38, 32.9, 27.4, 22.7), label = regions, hjust = 0, size = 2.5)
    )
  }
  c(region_key, list(
    annotate("point", x = 62.8, y = c(13, 9.6), shape = 1, size = c(6.6, 1.9), stroke = 0.3),
    annotate("text", x = 64.4, y = c(14.5, 10.2, 5.6), label = c("Voting", "eligible", "population"),
             hjust = 0, size = 2.5)
  ))
}

vitality_frame <- list(
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2),
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6.6, guide = "none"),

)
```

## Pie / doughnut (p.20)

The guide carries its own warning: "Use with caution. Should probably be
abandoned in favour of stacked bar if over 4 categories."

### The standard color order, one to six segments

```{r pie-order, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 150}
## Segment shares (%) traced from the guide's pies, clockwise from 12 o'clock. Names are
## colour-order positions; "O" is the guide's pale "Other". The last segment is always 44.4%.
pie_shares <- list(
  c(`1` = 55.6, O = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 55.6, `2` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 38.9, `2` = 16.7, `3` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 22.2, `2` = 20.3, `4` = 13.1, `3` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 22.2, `2` = 20.3, `5` = 7.4, `4` = 5.7, `3` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 15.6, `2` = 13.3, `5` = 10.2, `3` = 11.2, `4` = 5.3, `6` = 44.4)
)
pie_demo <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(pie_shares), function(i) {
  hi <- cumsum(pie_shares[[i]])
  data.frame(
    panel = as.character(i),
    key = names(hi),
    lo = hi - pie_shares[[i]],
    hi = unname(hi)
  )
}))

pie_grid <- function(hole) {
  ggplot(pie_demo, aes(xmin = hole, xmax = 1, ymin = .data$lo, ymax = .data$hi, fill = .data$key)) +
    geom_rect() +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(setNames(pal_pie(6), as.character(1:6)), O = "#CCD8DD"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_economist_2017("print") +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.2), hjust = 0.5),
      panel.spacing.x = unit(8, "pt")
    )
}

## Doughnut (hole) above, pie below -- the guide shows both rows.
pie_grid(0.52) + labs(title = "Standard colour order")
```

### "Naan bigger" -- a labeled doughnut

```{r naan, econ_height = 155}
## The guide labels its doughnuts directly, with a small colour block and a pale
## linking line to each segment. These are drawn in the guide's own coordinates
## (300 dpi pixels of the original chart) so the leader lines can be placed by hand.
donut_polygons <- function(values, cx, cy, r_out, r_in, n = 40) {
  edge <- 2 * pi * c(0, cumsum(values)) / sum(values)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(values), function(i) {
    arc <- seq(edge[i], edge[i + 1], length.out = n)
    data.frame(
      segment = names(values)[i],
      x = c(cx + r_out * sin(arc), cx + r_in * sin(rev(arc))),
      y = c(cy - r_out * cos(arc), cy - r_in * cos(rev(arc)))
    )
  }))
}
```

### "The scramble in Africa" -- two doughnuts, keyed labels

"Where linking lines get too crowded, key the labels with small colour
block" (p.20). The guide lists eleven trade partners and seven investment
sources: retain all of them rather than collapsing the smaller entries. Gray
takes "Rest of world"; repeated hues distinguish the remaining keyed labels.

```{r scramble, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 178}
## Drawn in the pixel coordinates of the guide's original, as for "Naan bigger".

  "China*" = 156.4, "United States" = 72.1, "France" = 61.6, "India" = 57.0, "Spain" = 48.1, "Italy" = 40.9,
  "Germany" = 40.4, "Britain" = 34.4, "Japan" = 25.3, "Brazil" = 25.3, "Rest of world" = 453.8
)
investment <- c(
  "Britain" = 7.5, "United States" = 3.7, "Italy" = 3.6, "China" = 2.5, "France" = 2.1, "India" = 1.8,
  "Rest of world" = 38.1
)
## The printed entries total $1,015.3bn, which the guide rounds to $1.02trn, and $59.3bn.
stopifnot(all.equal(sum(trade), 1015.3), all.equal(sum(investment), 59.3))

## Pie order 1-6 is blue, cyan, gold, teal, maroon, mint; the guide's trade key continues
## with mauve, dark green, olive and slate, and ends on the pale grey.

)

wedges$group <- paste(wedges$panel, wedges$segment)

}

  key_row("investment", "Rest of world", "Rest of world\n38.1", 770, 207, 750, investment_cols[7], 0)
)
```

## Double-scale charts (p.21)

"Double scales can be good at showing correlations and are economical with
space. But they can also be confusing/misleading." The guide asks for
colored y-axis labels in Econ Sans Cnd Regular rather than Light, so each
axis reads with its own series, and gives its own two-color orders: cyan and
teal for axis 1, maroon and mauve for axis 2.

`sec_axis()` is the mechanism: the second series is rescaled onto the first
axis, and `sec_axis()` inverts that transformation for the right-hand labels.
Both axes take `guide_axis_economist()`, which puts the labels inside the
panel. The axis titles still sit in a column beside the panel, so they are
broken over several short lines to keep that column narrow.

### "Out of steam" -- one line on each axis

```{r out-of-steam, econ_height = 175}
## Series traced from the guide: (x, y) are pixel positions in the original, converted
## to years and values from its gridlines (0 at y = 633, 70 at y = 264).
px_year <- function(x) 1955 + (x - 115) / 8
px_value <- function(y) (633 - y) / 5.27
track_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(115, 140, 155, 172, 190, 205, 220, 240, 300, 420, 430, 450, 470, 500, 520, 588),
  y = c(508, 509, 511, 520, 535, 548, 553, 557, 558, 558, 553, 553, 553, 553, 557, 556)
)
passengers_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(115, 131, 148, 160, 172, 190, 205, 220, 237, 250, 262, 272, 285, 298, 312, 322, 333, 340, 353, 365, 378,
        395, 410, 428, 440, 455, 470, 480, 490, 505, 520, 535, 548, 560, 575, 588),
  y = c(458, 442, 445, 452, 465, 467, 478, 482, 472, 485, 475, 470, 483, 475, 465, 478, 490, 480, 478, 470, 457,
        460, 468, 480, 465, 450, 430, 428, 420, 412, 390, 370, 360, 335, 318, 302)
)
rail <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "track", year = px_year(track_px$x), value = px_value(track_px$y)),
  data.frame(series = "passengers", year = px_year(passengers_px$x), value = px_value(passengers_px$y))
)
maroon <- pal_dot(6)[2]
cyan <- pal_dot(6)[1]
cyan_text <- "#2BADC4"
slate <- "#6B7F8C"

steam <- ggplot(rail, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_segment(
    x = 1994, xend = 1994, y = 0, yend = 64, linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.25, colour = slate
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 1994, y = 66.5, label = "Privatisation begins", size = 1.9, colour = slate) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(track = maroon, passengers = cyan), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist(),
    name = "National rail track\n'000 km", limits = c(0, 70), breaks = seq(0, 70, 10), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~., name = "Passenger kilometres\nbn", breaks = seq(0, 70, 10), guide = guide_axis_economist())
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1955, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2014),
    labels = c("1955", "70", "80", "90", "2000", "14"), limits = c(1945, 2022), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Out of steam", subtitle = "Britain, railways", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = maroon),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = maroon, hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  steam +
    labs(caption = "Source: Department for Transport"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### "Golden triangle" -- three lines on the left-hand axis

```{r golden-triangle, econ_height = 165}
## Series traced from the guide, as for "Out of steam": the left scale's gridlines are
## 0 at y = 591 and 100 at y = 222; the trade series is drawn on the left scale.
px_year <- function(x) 1994 + (x - 132) / 20.5
px_value <- function(y) (591 - y) / 3.69
trace <- function(series, xy) {
  data.frame(series = series, year = px_year(xy[[1]]), value = px_value(xy[[2]]))
}
nafta <- rbind(
  trace("Mexico", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500, 520, 540, 565),

  )),

    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500, 520, 540, 565),
    c(285, 292, 285, 282, 272, 266, 265, 264, 266, 270, 273, 277, 284, 296, 300, 308, 311, 314, 310, 306, 303, 302)
  )),
  trace("United States", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500, 520, 540, 565),
    c(471, 480, 478, 470, 463, 457, 455, 457, 455, 456, 455, 455, 462, 469, 473, 474, 471, 470, 469, 467, 464, 463)
  )),
  trace("Total trilateral trade", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 275, 295, 315, 335, 355, 375, 395, 415, 440, 462, 480, 500, 520, 545, 565),
    c(498, 483, 473, 460, 441, 431, 414, 388, 400, 403, 396, 375, 350, 327, 312, 299, 372, 312, 280, 265, 258, 244)
  ))
)

golden <- ggplot(nafta, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = .data$series == "Total trilateral trade")) +
```

### What to avoid

The guide illustrates three failure modes, reproduced here as the guide draws
them -- these are the charts *not* to copy. Its closing advice: "If you
cannot conform to the above rules try splitting the chart into panels or
indexing the variables."

```{r double-scale-avoid, econ_height = 155}
## Monthly series traced from the guide; the left scale (euro, $) is 1.0 at y = 473 and
## 1.4 at y = 210. The right scale (yields, %) runs 0-5, so the two do not share a zero.
px_euro <- function(y) 1 + (473 - y) / 660
months <- 2013.5 + (0:23) / 12
qe <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "Euro", year = months, value = px_euro(c(
    247, 245, 234, 236, 243, 250, 255, 268, 294, 310, 322, 333, 380, 397, 432, 432, 408, 405, 420, 411, 404, 404,
    438, 428
  ))),
  data.frame(series = "Italy", year = months, value = px_euro(c(
    284, 305, 324, 332, 344, 351, 367, 372, 392, 400, 392, 420, 430, 445, 465, 468, 450, 418, 402, 435, 420, 433,
    441, 458
  ))),
  data.frame(series = "Euro area", year = months[1:23], value = px_euro(c(
    337, 346, 358, 376, 380, 398, 406, 418, 427, 438, 442, 455, 465, 468, 486, 491, 458, 440, 450, 457, 450, 468,
    472
  )))
)
qe_cols <- c(Euro = pal_dot(6)[2], Italy = pal_dot(6)[5], `Euro area` = pal_dot(6)[1])
cyan_text <- "#2BADC4"

quantifying <- ggplot(qe, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.0, y = 1.24, label = "Italy", colour = pal_dot(6)[5], size = 2.4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.05, y = 1.03, label = "Euro area", colour = pal_dot(6)[1], size = 2.4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = qe_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist(),
    name = "Euro against the\ndollar, $ per €", limits = c(0.9, 1.4001), breaks = seq(1, 1.4, 0.1),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ (. - 0.9) * 10, name = "Ten-year government-\nbond yields, %", breaks = 0:5,
      guide = guide_axis_economist()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2015), labels = c("2014", "2015"), limits = c(2013.19, 2015.69), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Quantifying QE", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2]),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  quantifying +
    labs(caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"),
  media = "print"
)
```

```{r double-scale-avoid-2, econ_height = 155}
## Bars read off the guide (annual, 2002-15); the oil price is traced as (x, y) pixels,
## with the right scale 0 at y = 538 and 180 at y = 200 and one year = 33.7 px from x = 100.
beneath <- data.frame(
  year = 2002:2015,
  cash = c(27, 68, 75, 98, 79, 90, 91, -5, 32, 31, 18, -30, 1, -50)
)
brent_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(100, 130, 165, 190, 205, 225, 237, 258, 275, 285, 295, 302, 310, 318, 324, 340, 358, 375, 385, 395, 405,

  y = c(512, 495, 468, 455, 455, 420, 415, 430, 375, 370, 320, 290, 385, 470, 480, 420, 400, 415, 350, 320, 345,
        340, 320, 345, 335, 345, 340, 340, 345, 400, 440, 430, 455, 480, 460, 450)
)
brent <- data.frame(

## The right-hand scale is the left shifted by 60, so the two zero lines do not coincide.
lies <- ggplot() +

  ) +

    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2]),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 1)

economist_2017_chart(

    labs(caption = "Source: BCG"),
  media = "print"
```

```{r double-scale-avoid-3, econ_height = 165}
## Daily series traced from the guide: (x, y) pixels, with 6 rand at y = 228 and 30 px per
## rand, and one year = 55 px from x = 88 (the start of 2008).
rand_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(88, 95, 110, 125, 133, 140, 150, 160, 172, 185, 200, 215, 228, 240, 255, 270, 285, 300, 315, 330, 345,
        360, 375, 390, 405, 420, 435, 450, 465, 480, 495, 510, 520, 530, 540, 550, 560, 575, 582),
  y = c(258, 290, 290, 300, 375, 340, 360, 300, 290, 272, 275, 270, 265, 258, 262, 252, 262, 285, 282, 320, 310,
        325, 330, 345, 350, 375, 380, 385, 370, 395, 420, 470, 520, 550, 490, 470, 480, 460, 480)
)
sacci_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(88, 110, 125, 140, 150, 160, 172, 180, 200, 210, 225, 237, 250, 262, 272, 285, 300, 315, 330, 345, 360,
        375, 385, 395, 410, 420, 435, 445, 460, 475, 485, 500, 515, 525, 535, 545, 555, 570, 580),
  y = c(285, 295, 330, 300, 350, 330, 290, 300, 300, 290, 240, 235, 255, 230, 245, 270, 280, 285, 350, 330, 340,
        370, 365, 355, 350, 365, 348, 340, 360, 385, 345, 395, 410, 470, 490, 480, 455, 470, 475)
)
zuma <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "rand", year = 2008 + (rand_px$x - 88) / 55, value = 6 + (rand_px$y - 228) / 30),
  data.frame(series = "sacci", year = 2008 + (sacci_px$x - 88) / 55, value = 6 + (sacci_px$y - 228) / 30)
)
cyan_text <- "#2BADC4"

## An index value against an inverted currency scale: two disparate measures
## forced into visual correlation.
zuma_plot <- ggplot(zuma, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 12, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = c(rand = pal_dot(6)[2], sacci = pal_dot(6)[1]), guide = "none") +

    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  zuma_plot +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Thomson Reuters; SACCI"),
  media = "print"
)
```

## Blob heads (p.22)

"A secondary data variable added as area-sized bubbles or number boxes. Can
be used with column or thermometer charts."

### "The Big Mac index" -- numbers inside the bubbles

```{r big-mac, econ_height = 335}
## Values read off the guide's own marks (p.22 prints only the prices).
bigmac <- data.frame(
  country = c("Switzerland", "Norway", "Sweden", "Brazil", "United States",
              "Euro area", "Britain", "Japan", "Turkey", "China",
              "Vietnam", "India", "Mexico", "Russia"),
  y2016 = c(31, 6, 5, -32, -1, -19, -14, -37, -31, -46, -48, -61, -43, -68),
  y2017 = c(27, 14, 4, 2, 0, -19, -24, -35, -41, -43, -45, -50, -54, -57),
  price = c(6.4, 5.8, 5.3, 5.1, 5.1, 4.1, 3.8, 3.3, 3.0, 2.8, 2.6, 2.5, 2.3, 2.2)
)
bigmac$country <- factor(bigmac$country, levels = rev(bigmac$country))
bigmac_long <- data.frame(
  country = rep(bigmac$country, 2),
  year = rep(c("January 2016", "January 2017"), each = nrow(bigmac)),
  value = c(bigmac$y2016, bigmac$y2017)
)
## The guide fills its bubbles c22.5 k15 at 100% multiply: that colour
## multiplied into the chart's ground. The bubbles grow roughly linearly in
## diameter with the price, not in area.
blob_fill <- grDevices::rgb(t(grDevices::col2rgb(print_numberbox) * grDevices::col2rgb(print_bg) / 255),
                            maxColorValue = 255)
bigmac$bubble <- 4.4 + 0.72 * bigmac$price

## Footnote marks hang off the country names as superscripts.
bigmac_marks <- c("United States" = "\u2020", "Euro area" = "\u2021", "China" = "\u00a7", "India" = "**")
bigmac_labels <- function(x) {
  parse(text = ifelse(x %in% names(bigmac_marks),
                      paste0("'", x, "'^'", bigmac_marks[x], "'"),
                      paste0("'", x, "'")))
}

big_mac <- ggplot(bigmac, aes(y = country)) +
  ## Light rules across each row, stopping short of the bubble column.
  geom_segment(aes(x = -80, xend = 56, yend = country), colour = grid_col, linewidth = 0.18) +
  ## Each dumbbell's bar runs back to zero.
  geom_segment(aes(x = pmin(0, y2016, y2017), xend = pmax(0, y2016, y2017), yend = country),
               colour = "#66808E", linewidth = 0.34) +
  geom_linerange(
    data = bigmac_long,
    aes(x = value, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.2,
        ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.2, colour = year),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  ## The blob heads: the value inside, in 7pt (p.22).
  geom_point(aes(x = 66, size = bubble), colour = blob_fill, stroke = 0) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 66, label = format(price, nsmall = 1)), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt,
            colour = print_pal$text) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  ## The guide labels every 20; the fallback font is too wide for that at
  ## this width, so every other gridline goes unlabelled.
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(-85, 84),
                     breaks = seq(-80, 40, 20), labels = c("-80", "", "-40", "", "0", "", "40")) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = bigmac_labels) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "dot") +
  labs(
    title = "The Big Mac index",
    subtitle = paste0("Local currency under (-) / over (+)\nvaluation against the dollar, %\n",
                      "Right-hand figures: Big Mac price*, $"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE)

economist_2017_chart(
  big_mac +
    ## The footnote shares the caption's row, so the caption is padded to the
    ## footnote's seven lines to reserve the room.
    labs(caption = "Sources:\nMcDonald's;\nThe Economist"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = paste0("*At market exchange rates\n(Jan 11th 2017)\n\u2020Average of four cities\n",
                    "\u2021Weighted average of\nmember countries\n\u00a7Average of five cities\n**Maharaja Mac")
)
```

### "Up in the air" -- bubbles and numbers outside the bar

"To avoid awkward alignment, if most numbers won't fit, put them outside
bubble and align text right."

```{r up-in-air, econ_height = 254}
## Bar lengths are read off the guide's bars; the bubble values are printed.
travel <- data.frame(
  country = c("China", "India", "Germany", "Spain", "United States", "Britain",
              "South Korea", "Canada", "Brazil", "France", "Italy", "Australia",
              "Japan", "Netherlands", "Russia"),
  change = c(16.5, 9.7, 7.6, 6.7, 5.4, 5.4, 3.9, 3.8, 3.7, 2.0, 1.3, 1.3, 1.1, -1.7, -6.6),
  bn = c(261, 26, 58, 18, 288, 44, 32, 23, 32, 36, 31, 21, 62, 18, 21)
)
travel$country <- factor(travel$country, levels = rev(travel$country))

air <- ggplot(travel, aes(country, change)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = change < 0), width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  ## Bubbles sized by area, with the value set to their right.
  geom_point(aes(y = 22.2, size = bn), colour = blob_fill, stroke = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 31.5, label = bn), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt, hjust = 1,
            colour = print_pal$text) +
  ## The "$bn" key sits above the axis, pointing at the bubbles.
  annotate("rect", xmin = 16.1, xmax = 17.1, ymin = 18.8, ymax = 31.5, fill = blob_fill) +
  annotate("polygon", x = c(16.1, 15.7, 16.1), y = c(23.6, 25.1, 26.6), fill = blob_fill) +
  annotate("text", x = 16.6, y = 25.1, label = "$bn", size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text) +
  ## Fixed limits keep the key above the axis out of the panel's range.
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 15.5), ylim = c(-10.5, 31.7), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pal_bar(2)[1], `TRUE` = pal_bar(2)[2])) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7.3) +
  ## "-10" and "-5" run together in the fallback font; leave -5 unlabelled.
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right",
                     breaks = seq(-10, 15, 5), labels = c("-10", "", "0", "5", "10", "15")) +
  labs(
    title = "Up in the air",
    subtitle = "Business travel spending, 2014\n% change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE)

economist_2017_chart(
  air +
    labs(caption = "Source: GBTA"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### "Starting small" -- equal-sized number blocks

"If number range or positive / negative values rule out bubbles, revert to
equal-sized number blocks."

```{r starting-small, econ_height = 175}
## Bar lengths are read off the guide's bars; the market caps are printed.
exchanges <- data.frame(
  exchange = rep(c("Johannesburg", "Nigeria", "Mauritius", "Nairobi", "Namibia", "BRVM*"), 2),
  listing = rep(c("Domestic", "Foreign"), each = 6),
  listed = c(306, 176, 75, 65, 8, 41, 71, 0, 0, 0, 33, 0)
)
exchanges$exchange <- factor(exchanges$exchange, levels = rev(unique(exchanges$exchange)))
exchanges$listing <- factor(exchanges$listing, levels = c("Foreign", "Domestic"))
caps <- data.frame(
  exchange = factor(levels(exchanges$exchange), levels = levels(exchanges$exchange)),
  cap = c(11.6, 2.3, 19.9, 6.2, 29.3, 943)
)

small <- ggplot(exchanges, aes(exchange, listed)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = listing), width = 0.65) +
  ## Equal-sized blocks, right-aligned, rather than area-sized bubbles: 9pt
  ## tall and 15pt wide.
  geom_tile(data = caps, aes(y = 500, height = 82), width = 0.6, fill = blob_fill) +
  geom_text(data = caps, aes(y = 500, label = cap), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text) +
  ## The "Market cap, $bn" key, pointing at the last block.
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.58, xmax = 1.42, ymin = 119, ymax = 421, fill = blob_fill) +
  annotate("polygon", x = c(0.78, 1, 1.22), y = c(421, 445, 421), fill = blob_fill) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 270, label = "Market cap, $bn", size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 6.55), ylim = c(0, 548), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Domestic = pal_bar(2)[2], Foreign = pal_bar(2)[1]),
                    limits = c("Domestic", "Foreign")) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", breaks = seq(0, 400, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "Starting small",
    subtitle = "Number of companies\nlisted on stock exchanges\nOctober 2016",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE) +
  ## The key sits at the right of the subtitle, which a negative margin tucks up into.
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "right", legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -28, b = 0))

economist_2017_chart(
  small +
    labs(caption = "Source: World Federation\nof Exchanges"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*West African\nregional exchange"
)
```

## Miscellaneous styling (p.25)

### Number boxes

"Use where multiple charts are referenced in text." A 7.5pt bold numeral on
the number-box fill, top right.

```{r number-box, econ_height = 165}
numbered <- tokyo +
  labs(caption = NULL)

economist_2017_chart(
  numbered +
    labs(caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"),
  media = "print",
  number = 1
)
```

### Highlight panels

"For secondary information, like forecast or estimate, use neutral style."

```{r highlight-neutral, econ_height = 165}
## Read off the guide's lines at five-year intervals; every country is 100 in 2015.
jobs <- data.frame(
  year = rep(seq(1950, 2100, by = 5), 4),
  place = rep(c("Japan", "United States", "European Union", "China"), each = 31),
  index = c(
    65, 71, 77, 86, 93, 98, 102, 106, 111, 112, 111, 109, 105, 100, 96, 93, 89, 85, 79, 75, 72, 69, 67, 65, 63, 62, 60,
    59, 58, 56, 56,
    48, 50, 53, 56, 61, 66, 71, 75, 78, 83, 89, 94, 97, 100, 101, 102, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 111, 112, 113, 115, 116,
    117, 118, 119, 119, 119,
    76, 78, 80, 83, 85, 88, 91, 95, 97, 98, 99, 101, 102, 100, 98, 96, 94, 91, 89, 87, 85, 83, 82, 81, 81, 80, 79, 78,
    77, 76, 76,
    34, 35, 36, 39, 45, 51, 58, 67, 75, 81, 86, 94, 99, 100, 100, 98, 96, 90, 86, 83, 79, 73, 69, 67, 65, 63, 59, 57,
    55, 54, 53
  )
)
jobs$place <- factor(jobs$place, levels = c("China", "European Union", "Japan", "United States"))
## Four labels set in the panel, as in the guide, in place of a key.
job_labels <- data.frame(
  year = c(1971, 2029, 2095, 1989), index = c(112, 115, 91, 49),
  label = c("Japan", "United\nStates", "European\nUnion", "China")
)

fill_jobs <- ggplot(jobs, aes(year, index, colour = place)) +
  ## The forecast panel: neutral fill, with a 1pt rule across its top.
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2015, xmax = 2100, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 137, fill = print_highlight) +
  annotate("segment", x = 2015, xend = 2100, y = 137, yend = 137, colour = "#66808E", linewidth = 0.35) +
  annotate("text", x = 2058, y = 130.5, label = "FORECAST", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
           colour = "#66808E") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = job_labels, aes(year, index, label = label), colour = print_pal$text, size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt,
            lineheight = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ## The 5pt black circle on the index point.
  geom_point(data = data.frame(year = 2015, index = 100), aes(year, index), colour = "black",
             size = 5 / 0.75 / ggplot2::.pt, stroke = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(20, 137),
                     breaks = seq(20, 120, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1933, 2141), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(1950, 2100, 25),
                     minor_breaks = seq(1950, 2100, 5), labels = economist_year_format(),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "line_side") +
  labs(
    title = "Who will fill the jobs?",
    subtitle = "Working-age population*, 2015=100",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

economist_2017_chart(
  fill_jobs +
    labs(caption = "Source: United Nations\nPopulation Division"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Aged 15-64"
)
```

### Highlight labels

"Use to mark specific dates and points on axis" -- a 0.5pt red rule with a
7pt label. "If there are only 1 or 2 points, and they are key to the chart
meaning, use colour/medium font."

```{r highlight-labels, econ_height = 155}
## The guide's line, read off at weekly intervals (the guide's own shape).

  t = seq(2015, by = 1 / 60, length.out = 122),
  price = c(
    510, 505, 495, 485, 475, 470, 475, 480, 485, 490, 490, 485, 480, 500, 510, 515, 500, 490, 490, 490, 485,
    460, 450, 425, 420, 430, 440, 440, 435, 430, 415, 400, 385, 380, 380, 380, 375, 375, 380, 375, 365, 345,
    335, 320, 315, 315, 320, 330, 340, 340, 340, 330, 315, 300, 290, 295, 300, 290, 260, 255, 235, 240, 230,
    220, 210, 200, 185, 180, 170, 180, 190, 195, 200, 195, 205, 210, 210, 220, 235, 240, 230, 225, 225, 230,
    245, 260, 275, 290, 285, 285, 280, 285, 290, 295, 285, 275, 265, 280, 285, 305, 320, 330, 320, 320, 330,
    340, 355, 360, 370, 380, 375, 380, 385, 395, 410, 430, 445, 460, 425, 360, 335, 270
  )
)
## Each event: a 0.5pt rule from the labelled point down to the axis, and its label.
events <- data.frame(
  t = c(2015.396, 2015.542, 2015.983, 2016.31, 2016.967),

  label = c("Accounting\nscandal", "CEO resigns", "$4.6bn\nrecord loss", "Westinghouse\nWrite-down",
            "CB&I Stone\n& Webster\nwrite-down"),
  ## Labels sit just right of their rules, top-aligned with the point, except
  ## the fourth, which hangs below its point, and the last, centred on its rule.

  hjust = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5),

)

woes_chart <- ggplot(toshiba, aes(t, price)) +
  geom_segment(data = events, aes(x = t, xend = t, y = 0, yend = top), colour = crisis_ink, linewidth = 0.234,
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = events, aes(t, top), colour = crisis_ink, size = 0.9, stroke = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

                     minor_breaks = seq(2015, 2017, by = 1 / 12), labels = c("2015", "16", "17"),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
```

### Truncated year labels

Every dated axis in the guide truncates years to two digits, keeping the
first label and each century boundary in full -- `1948 52 56 ... 96 2000 04`
(pp.6, 7, 13, 15, 16, 23). `economist_year_format()` does this, so the charts
above need not spell their `labels` out by hand:

```{r year-labels}
economist_year(seq(1948, 2016, 4))
```

### Broken scales

"Use when breaking y-axis on line, thermometer and scatter charts. Not needed
on indexed, negative scale or inverted scales" (p.25). The mark is decoration
only: truncate the axis with `limits` as usual, then add
`geom_scale_break()` to declare it. The guide never excises a band from the
middle of an axis, so nothing here rescales the data.

The guide's other rule is emphatic: **don't break the scale on a bar or
column chart -- use a thermometer instead.** A truncated bar misstates the
comparison the bar exists to make.

```{r broken-scale, econ_height = 155}
broken <- ggplot(merkel, aes(t, approval)) +
  geom_line(colour = pal_line(1), linewidth = 0.8) +
  ## Black, 0.4pt stroke, 6pt wide, centred between the baseline and the
  ## lowest tick -- the guide's own specification.
  geom_scale_break() +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist(), position = "right", limits = c(24, 80),
                     breaks = seq(30, 80, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2003.8, 2018.3), expand = c(0, 0),
                     breaks = c(2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2016),
                     minor_breaks = 2005:2016, labels = economist_year_format(),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE, cap = "upper")) +
  labs(
    title = "Mutti's malaise",
    subtitle = "German approval of Angela\nMerkel, % polled",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print")

economist_2017_chart(
  broken +
    labs(caption = "Source: ARD DeutschlandTREND/infratest dimap"),
  media = "print"
)
```

## What this vignette does not reproduce

* **Econ Sans itself (p.5).** The guide's typefaces are licensed and not
  distributable, so the figures use the `"sans"` fallback: the type *sizes*
  match the guide but the letterforms do not, and medium, regular and light
  are all drawn plain. See the Typefaces section for passing a close free
  substitute through `base_family`.
* **Tables (p.19)** are not a `ggplot2` geom. The guide's table specification
  -- 7.5/9 medium headline, 7.5/9 light body, alternating row fills, 3pt
  internal padding -- belongs to a table package such as `gt` or `flextable`.
* **Timelines (pp.23-24)** are annotation layouts rather than a chart type:
  the data layer is an ordinary line or column chart, which the sections
  above already cover, and everything that makes them timelines is hand-placed
  text, rules and period bars. The mobile variants (p.24) are a layout
  problem rather than a plotting one.
* **Exact publication placement.** The leader, Espresso and panel examples
  above reproduce the guide's type sizes, outer margins, fixed blank area and
  panel gutter. Their placement inside an Economist article remains a
  publication-layout concern rather than a `ggplot2` theme element.
